title: Ecosystems & Material Cycles
welcome_lead: Today's adventure: Ecosystems & Material Cycles — food webs, energy flow and nutrient cycling.
meta_desc: GCSE Biology adventure on ecosystems, food webs and nutrient cycles.
final_note: You linked feeding relationships and material cycles from ecology.

concepts.def: All organisms in an area plus their environment
Organism making its own food by photosynthesis
Organism that eats other organisms for energy
Microbe breaking down dead material to recycle nutrients
Living factor in an ecosystem (e.g. predators)

walkthroughs.body_html:
Energy enters at the producer via sunlight.

Arrows point in the direction of energy flow. Roughly 10% passes to each next trophic level — the rest lost as heat, waste and respiration.

Plants take CO₂ from air via photosynthesis. Respiration, combustion and decay return it.

Burning fossil fuels has raised atmospheric CO₂ — a key driver of climate change.

Water: evaporation → condensation → precipitation → runoff/percolation.

Nitrogen: fixing bacteria turn N₂ into nitrates; plants absorb nitrates; decomposers recycle nitrogen from dead matter.

mcqs.q: Roughly what % of energy transfers between trophic levels?
Which organisms convert nitrogen gas to nitrates?
options: Nitrogen-fixing bacteria
Plants
Decomposer fungi
Herbivores

mcqs.q: Where do plants get most of their biomass from?
options: From carbon dioxide in the air — the carbon in plant tissue comes mostly from CO2 fixed during photosynthesis.
Plants gain most of their mass directly from sunlight, which has weight.
Plants get most of their mass from the soil through their roots.
Larger animals always eat the next ones up, and there aren't enough giant animals.

mcqs.q: Why are food chains usually limited to about 4 or 5 trophic levels?
options: Only ~10 percent of energy is transferred between trophic levels; eventually too little energy remains to support another level.
Plants gain most of their mass directly from sunlight, which has weight.
Larger animals always eat the next ones up, and there aren't enough giant animals.
There aren't enough types of animals to fill more trophic levels.

mcqs.q: What is the main role of mitochondria in a cell?
options: Plants gain most of their mass directly from sunlight, which has weight.
To carry out aerobic respiration, producing ATP that cells use as an energy currency.
Mitochondria store sunlight and release it for photosynthesis.
Mitochondria produce energy by creating it from nothing.

Living factor in an ecosystem (e.g. predators)
Organism that eats other organisms for energy
Organism making its own food by photosynthesis

mcqs.q: Producers take in 10000 kJ. Roughly how much reaches the primary consumer (kJ)?
Producers in a meadow take in 20000 kJ of energy. Using the 10% rule, roughly how much energy is available to the primary consumers?
options: 200 kJ

mcqs.q: Which process in the carbon cycle removes carbon dioxide from the atmosphere?
options: Photosynthesis
Respiration
Combustion
Decomposition

mcqs.q: Nitrogen-fixing bacteria are important in the nitrogen cycle because they:
options: Convert nitrogen gas into nitrogen compounds plants can use
Turn nitrates back into nitrogen gas
Break down proteins into ammonia
Absorb nitrates into plant roots

mcqs.q: Why is decomposition slower in cold, waterlogged soil?
options: Decomposers are less active without warmth and oxygen.
There are too many nutrients for decomposers.
Cold water speeds up microbial respiration.
Decomposers do not need oxygen at all.
